status: Agreed 20 Nov 2026. Deadline Thursday 26 November 2026 (confirmed). Dates compressed on 20 Nov after a 3-day slip; the bonus phase is only if time allows.
principles: Every data transformation is a committed script; raw files stay as downloaded.
Any choice the results could steer (cleaning rules, features, number of clusters, thresholds) is written in notes/ and committed before the run it governs.
Your Mac is the run of record; the cloud builds and tests code and cross-checks results.
Nothing is decided without you: each stage opens with the questions it needs answered.
The report is yours; Claude supplies code, numbers, figures and checks, never report text.

phases.name: Set-up
steps: GitHub repository (done)
File-selection rule (PR #1)
Skeleton and download stage (PR #2)
rules_first: notes/data-selection.md (written)

phases.name: Download and load
steps: Download the 26 selected files on your Mac (about 1.6 GB) with a manifest
Loader: read every column as text, map columns by header name (column order changes between files), keep station ids as text
Typed Parquet copy made by code
Checks: row counts per file, unique trip id, the two overlap days (14 May, 15 June)
Optional: station coordinates from TfL BikePoint (your Mac; blocked from the cloud)
you: Run the download and loader on your Mac and paste the output

phases.name: Cleaning
steps: Write notes/cleaning-rules.md and commit it before cleaning
Apply each rule in order and count what it removes
Station id/name consistency table
rules_first: What counts as a 2025 trip (start date? trips over midnight on 31 Dec)
Missing stations
Zero or negative durations
Very long durations (keep, cap or drop?)
Round trips (start = end): drop for the graph? keep for profiles?
Duplicate trip ids from the overlap days
Inconsistent station names or ids
you: Approve the cleaning rules before they run

phases.name: Description
steps: Total trips, active stations, start/end stations
Trips per day, per station, per weekday and hour; duration distribution
Figures in the agreed style (Okabe–Ito colours, units in labels)
rules_first: Definition of an 'active' station
you: Comment on the results in your report

phases.name: Station profiles
steps: Global feature table (the 12 brief features)
Hourly profile (24 departure + 24 arrival shares), weekday/weekend profile, monthly profile
Per-station daily and weekly series
rules_first: Morning and evening hour windows
Minimum activity for a station to be profiled
Counts vs shares, log transform, standardisation

phases.name: Dimension reduction
steps: PCA on each profile: scree plot, loadings or correlation circle, station map
One non-linear method from the course: Isomap or t-SNE (visualisation only, never clustered on, per DR s63)
rules_first: Which profile(s) feed the main analysis
Non-linear method and its parameters (k for Isomap; perplexity for t-SNE)

phases.name: Clustering of profiles
steps: k-means (k-means++, many restarts, seed 42)
Gaussian mixture with BIC
Optional Ward hierarchical clustering as a cross-check
Cluster profiles and a map (needs station coordinates)
rules_first: Rule for K (e.g. BIC for the GMM; silhouette or Calinski–Harabasz for k-means), fixed before running

phases.name: Anomalies
steps: Robust Mahalanobis (MCD) on the first PCA components
LOF and/or isolation forest
Stations badly represented by their cluster (silhouette, distance to centroid)
Interpretation table: error, special station, tourist, network edge, rare but plausible
rules_first: Score thresholds or top-N to examine
you: Interpret the anomalies in your report

phases.name: Origin–destination graph
steps: Directed weighted graph, weights = 2025 trips i → j
Nodes, arcs, in/out-degree, strength and weight distributions
Centrality (e.g. PageRank, betweenness) and in/out imbalance
Optional: morning vs evening, weekday vs weekend graphs
rules_first: Round trips (self-loops) in or out
Which centrality measures

phases.name: SBM
phases.course: not covered in the slides you shared
steps: Directed Poisson (count) SBM on the trip matrix
Number of blocks by ICL, fixed as the rule before running
Block sizes, block-to-block flow matrix, emitter/receiver roles
Optional cross-check: Louvain or spectral clustering on the symmetrised graph
rules_first: SBM variant (plain or degree-corrected) and the rule for the number of blocks
you: D10: Python route for the SBM, needed by 23 Nov (after you check the course material)

phases.name: Comparison
steps: Contingency table vector clusters × SBM blocks
ARI and NMI
Side-by-side maps

phases.name: Bonus (if time)
steps: Maps of clusters and blocks
UK bank holidays and/or weather (outside data reduced by code)
Temporal stability: SBM or communities per month, ARI between months
rules_first: Which outside data, chosen before looking at results

phases.name: Packaging
steps: run_all end to end on your Mac; md5 of the main output in README
Code cleanup (comments removed, checked by syntax-tree comparison)
README followed literally from a clean copy in a fresh venv
ZIP under 25 MB from committed files, tested by unzipping and running

phases.name: Report
steps: You write it. Claude supplies numbers, figures, fact checks and APA references on request.
